I've come up with a clear rule for filling rows and columns. For each row that intersects the original block, I’ll fill in the direction away from any markers in that row. entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC rule: extend a solid rectangle away from marker dots', path='continual-arc', global_=True, content='''For ARC grids containing one solid rectangular block (often color 2) and isolated marker dots outside it (often another color), extend the block along its rows and columns toward grid edges, while preserving the marker dots. For each row intersecting the rectangle, look for marker dots in that row outside the rectangle: a marker to the left means extend the rectangle across to the right edge (away from that marker); a marker to the right means extend leftward; with no aligned side marker, extend both ways to both edges. Likewise for each column intersecting the rectangle: a marker above means extend downward only, a marker below means extend upward only, and no aligned marker means extend both ways to the edges. The original rectangle stays filled. Markers are not overwritten. This rule was validated against three demonstrations and solved task-85237f27 with zero wrong submissions. Demonstrations showed same-row left/right markers and top/bottom markers; behavior for markers on both sides of one line was not observed.''')
print(entry)
